question: 0.3.3: can conversations that together need more KV cells than the unified pool holds wait for room instead of failing every request of the step, without changing anything when the pool has room?
machine: GMKtec EVO-X2 class, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151), 128 GB, 96 GB carve
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, MTP draft head IQ4_XS
why: a user's eight agents held ~870K tokens in a 680K-cell q8_0 pool (8 slots); upstream halves a batch that does not fit down to one token, then fails every request running at that moment with 'Context size has been exceeded' and clears their caches: seven failed at once
what: patches/apply_pool_guard_033.py: a prompt starts only when it fits beside what the busy conversations will hold - their whole prompts and a reserve for each answer (8192 tokens, less when the request allows less) - once idle conversations are on disk or purged; until then it waits in the queue holding no slot, and one that has waited a minute holds back those behind it. A prompt's next piece and an answer's next tokens take only the cells there are, idle slots purged first, else wait. When every busy conversation waits three steps in a row, the one that arrived last gives way: a prompt holding cells with a 503, else an answer ending with stop_type limit. /slots answers with X-Strix-Waiting; the app's Logs page shows the requests waiting. STRIX_POOL_GUARD=0 restores 0.3.2
probe: tmp/rel033/pool_probe.py (thinking off, temperature 0.7, distinct text per conversation, nothing shared)
